definition: Lyra is a lossy audio codec developed by Google that is designed for compressing speech at very low bitrates.
details: Unlike most other audio formats, it compresses data using a machine learning-based algorithm.
story: Think of a grammar teacher who never memorized a rule but can still tell you when a sentence sounds wrong. The machine learns language the way you did — by hearing so much of it that the patterns sink in. It figures out meaning by noticing which words like to travel together. The machine learns to read between the lines by reading an impossible number of lines. That pattern-earned fluency is Lyra (codec).
